passages.text: Behold what manner of love the Father has given to us, that we should be called children of God. And that is what we are! The reason the world does not know us is that it did not know Him.
passages.sermon:
God is our Father.
God has given us great love.
God calls us His children.
We are truly children of God.
The world does not know us.
The world does not know us because it did not know God.
passages.original: Ἴδετε ποταπὴν ἀγάπην δέδωκεν ἡμῖν ὁ Πατὴρ ἵνα τέκνα Θεοῦ κληθῶμεν καὶ ἐσμέν διὰ τοῦτο ὁ κόσμος οὐ γινώσκει ἡμᾶς ὅτι οὐκ ἔγνω αὐτόν

passages.text: Beloved, we are now children of God, and what we will be has not yet been revealed. We know that when Christ appears, we will be like Him, for we will see Him as He is.
passages.sermon:
We are children of God now.
God has made us His children.
We do not know what we will become in the future.
God has not shown us yet what we will be.
We know one thing.
When Christ appears, we will be like Christ.
We will see Christ as He truly is.
passages.original: Ἀγαπητοί νῦν τέκνα Θεοῦ ἐσμεν καὶ οὔπω ἐφανερώθη τί ἐσόμεθα οἴδαμεν ὅτι ἐὰν φανερωθῇ ὅμοιοι αὐτῷ ἐσόμεθα ὅτι ὀψόμεθα αὐτὸν καθώς ἐστιν

passages.text: And everyone who has this hope in Him purifies himself, just as Christ is pure.
passages.sermon: Everyone who has this hope in Christ purifies himself.\r\nChrist is pure.\r\n
passages.original: καὶ πᾶς ὁ ἔχων τὴν ἐλπίδα ταύτην ἐπ’ αὐτῷ ἁγνίζει ἑαυτὸν καθὼς ἐκεῖνος ἁγνός ἐστιν

passages.text: Everyone who practices sin practices lawlessness as well. Indeed, sin is lawlessness.
passages.sermon: Everyone who practices sin also practices lawlessness.\r\nSin is lawlessness.
passages.original: Πᾶς ὁ ποιῶν τὴν ἁμαρτίαν καὶ τὴν ἀνομίαν ποιεῖ καὶ ἡ ἁμαρτία ἐστὶν ἡ ἀνομία

passages.text: But you know that Christ appeared to take away sins, and in Him there is no sin.
passages.sermon:
Christ is the Son of God.
You know that Christ appeared.
He came to take away sins.
There is no sin in Christ.
passages.original: καὶ οἴδατε ὅτι ἐκεῖνος ἐφανερώθη ἵνα τὰς ἁμαρτίας ἄρῃ καὶ ἁμαρτία ἐν αὐτῷ οὐκ ἔστιν

passages.text: No one who remains in Him keeps on sinning. No one who continues to sin has seen Him or known Him.
passages.sermon:
Jesus Christ is without sin.
Anyone who remains in Jesus does not keep on sinning.
Anyone who keeps on sinning has not seen Jesus.
Anyone who keeps on sinning does not know Jesus.
passages.original: πᾶς ὁ ἐν αὐτῷ μένων οὐχ ἁμαρτάνει πᾶς ὁ ἁμαρτάνων οὐχ ἑώρακεν αὐτὸν οὐδὲ ἔγνωκεν αὐτόν

passages.text: Little children, let no one deceive you: The one who practices righteousness is righteous, just as Christ is righteous.
passages.sermon:
John addresses believers as "little children."
\r\nHe warns them not to let anyone deceive them.
\r\nAnyone who practices righteousness is righteous.
\r\nChrist is righteous.
\r\nThe one who practices righteousness is righteous in the same way Christ is righteous.
passages.original: Τεκνία μηδεὶς πλανάτω ὑμᾶς ὁ ποιῶν τὴν δικαιοσύνην δίκαιός ἐστιν καθὼς ἐκεῖνος δίκαιός ἐστιν

passages.text: The one who practices sin is of the devil, because the devil has been sinning from the very start. This is why the Son of God was revealed, to destroy the works of the devil.
passages.sermon:
Anyone who practices sin belongs to the devil.
The devil has been sinning from the very beginning.
The Son of God appeared for this reason.
He came to destroy the works of the devil.
passages.original: ὁ ποιῶν τὴν ἁμαρτίαν ἐκ τοῦ διαβόλου ἐστίν ὅτι ἀπ’ ἀρχῆς ὁ διάβολος ἁμαρτάνει εἰς τοῦτο ἐφανερώθη ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ Θεοῦ ἵνα λύσῃ τὰ ἔργα τοῦ διαβόλου

passages.text: Anyone born of God refuses to practice sin, because God’s seed abides in him; he cannot go on sinning, because he has been born of God.
passages.sermon:
Anyone born of God does not practice sin.
God’s seed remains in that person.
This person cannot continue sinning.
He has been born of God.
passages.original: Πᾶς ὁ γεγεννημένος ἐκ τοῦ Θεοῦ ἁμαρτίαν οὐ ποιεῖ ὅτι σπέρμα αὐτοῦ ἐν αὐτῷ μένει καὶ οὐ δύναται ἁμαρτάνειν ὅτι ἐκ τοῦ Θεοῦ γεγέννηται

passages.text: By this the children of God are distinguished from the children of the devil: Anyone who does not practice righteousness is not of God, nor is anyone who does not love his brother.
passages.sermon:
God has children.
The devil also has children.
We can tell who belongs to God and who belongs to the devil.
Anyone who does not do what is right does not come from God.
Anyone who does not love his brother does not come from God.
passages.original: ἐν τούτῳ φανερά ἐστιν τὰ τέκνα τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ τὰ τέκνα τοῦ διαβόλου πᾶς ὁ μὴ ποιῶν δικαιοσύνην οὐκ ἔστιν ἐκ τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ ὁ μὴ ἀγαπῶν τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ

passages.text: This is the message you have heard from the beginning: We should love one another.
passages.sermon:
God gave a message from the beginning.
You have heard this message from the start.
The message is clear.
We should love one another.
passages.original: Ὅτι αὕτη ἐστὶν ἡ ἀγγελία ἣν ἠκούσατε ἀπ’ ἀρχῆς ἵνα ἀγαπῶμεν ἀλλήλους

passages.text: Do not be like Cain, who belonged to the evil one and murdered his brother. And why did Cain slay him? Because his own deeds were evil, while those of his brother were righteous.
passages.sermon:
Cain belonged to the evil one.
Cain killed his brother.
Do not be like Cain.
Cain killed his brother because his own deeds were evil.
His brother’s deeds were righteous.
passages.original: οὐ καθὼς Κάϊν ἐκ τοῦ πονηροῦ ἦν καὶ ἔσφαξεν τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ καὶ χάριν τίνος ἔσφαξεν αὐτόν ὅτι τὰ ἔργα αὐτοῦ πονηρὰ ἦν τὰ δὲ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ αὐτοῦ δίκαια

passages.text: So do not be surprised, brothers, if the world hates you.
passages.sermon:
Brothers, I speak to you.
Do not be surprised.
The world may hate you.
This is true for followers of Jesus.
Do not wonder when this happens.
passages.original: καὶ Μὴ θαυμάζετε ἀδελφοί εἰ μισεῖ ὑμᾶς ὁ κόσμος

passages.text: We know that we have passed from death to life, because we love our brothers. The one who does not love remains in death.
passages.sermon:
We know this truth.
We have moved from death to life.
We know this because we love our brothers.
Anyone who does not love stays in death.
passages.original: Ἡμεῖς οἴδαμεν ὅτι μεταβεβήκαμεν ἐκ τοῦ θανάτου εἰς τὴν ζωήν ὅτι ἀγαπῶμεν τοὺς ἀδελφούς ὁ μὴ ἀγαπῶν μένει ἐν τῷ θανάτῳ

passages.text: Everyone who hates his brother is a murderer, and you know that eternal life does not reside in a murderer.
passages.sermon: Everyone who hates his brother is a murderer.\r\nA murderer does not have eternal life in him.\r\nYou know this.
passages.original: πᾶς ὁ μισῶν τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ ἀνθρωποκτόνος ἐστίν καὶ οἴδατε ὅτι πᾶς ἀνθρωποκτόνος οὐκ ἔχει ζωὴν αἰώνιον ἐν αὐτῷ μένουσαν

passages.text: By this we know what love is: Jesus laid down His life for us, and we ought to lay down our lives for our brothers.
passages.sermon:
Jesus showed us what love is.
He laid down His life for us.
We know love because of His sacrifice.
We ought to lay down our lives for our brothers.
passages.original: Ἐν τούτῳ ἐγνώκαμεν τὴν ἀγάπην ὅτι ἐκεῖνος ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ ἔθηκεν καὶ ἡμεῖς ὀφείλομεν ὑπὲρ τῶν ἀδελφῶν τὰς ψυχὰς θεῖναι

passages.text: If anyone with earthly possessions sees his brother in need, but withholds his compassion from him, how can the love of God abide in him?
passages.sermon:
A person may have the things of this world.
He may see his brother in need.
He may close his heart to his brother.
If he does this, he withholds compassion.
The love of God cannot remain in such a person.
passages.original: ὃς δ’ ἂν ἔχῃ τὸν βίον τοῦ κόσμου καὶ θεωρῇ τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ χρείαν ἔχοντα καὶ κλείσῃ τὰ σπλάγχνα αὐτοῦ ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ πῶς ἡ ἀγάπη τοῦ Θεοῦ μένει ἐν αὐτῷ

passages.text: Little children, let us love not in word and speech, but in action and truth.
passages.sermon:
John addresses believers as little children.
He urges them to love one another.
He says, do not love only with words.
Do not love only with speech.
Love with your actions.
Love with truth.
passages.original: Τεκνία μὴ ἀγαπῶμεν λόγῳ μηδὲ τῇ γλώσσῃ ἀλλὰ ἐν ἔργῳ καὶ ἀληθείᾳ

passages.text: And by this we will know that we belong to the truth, and will assure our hearts in His presence: Even if our hearts condemn us, God is greater than our hearts, and He knows all things.
passages.sermon:
God knows everything.
God is greater than our hearts.
Sometimes our hearts condemn us.
Even then, God is greater than our hearts.
We can assure our hearts before God.
We will know that we belong to the truth by this.
We will have confidence in His presence.
passages.original: καὶ ἐν τούτῳ γνωσόμεθα ὅτι ἐκ τῆς ἀληθείας ἐσμέν καὶ ἔμπροσθεν αὐτοῦ πείσομεν τὴν καρδίαν ἡμῶν ὅτι ἐὰν καταγινώσκῃ ἡμῶν ἡ καρδία ὅτι μείζων ἐστὶν ὁ Θεὸς τῆς καρδίας ἡμῶν καὶ γινώσκει πάντα

passages.text: Beloved, if our hearts do not condemn us, we have confidence before God, and we will receive from Him whatever we ask, because we keep His commandments and do what is pleasing in His sight.
passages.sermon:
Beloved, I speak to you as followers of Jesus Christ.
If our hearts do not condemn us, we have confidence before God.
We can come to God without fear.
We receive from God whatever we ask.
We keep His commandments.
We do what pleases Him.
passages.original: Ἀγαπητοί ἐὰν ἡ καρδία ἡμῶν μὴ καταγινώσκῃ παρρησίαν ἔχομεν πρὸς τὸν Θεόν καὶ ὃ ἐὰν αἰτῶμεν λαμβάνομεν ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ ὅτι τὰς ἐντολὰς αὐτοῦ τηροῦμεν καὶ τὰ ἀρεστὰ ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ ποιοῦμεν

passages.text: And this is His commandment: that we should believe in the name of His Son, Jesus Christ, and we should love one another just as He commanded us.
passages.sermon:
God gives us a commandment.
God commands us to believe in the name of His Son.
His Son is Jesus Christ.
God also commands us to love one another.
God told us to do this.
passages.original: καὶ αὕτη ἐστὶν ἡ ἐντολὴ αὐτοῦ ἵνα πιστεύσωμεν τῷ ὀνόματι τοῦ Υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ ἀγαπῶμεν ἀλλήλους καθὼς ἔδωκεν ἐντολὴν ἡμῖν

passages.text: Whoever keeps His commandments remains in God, and God in him. And by this we know that He remains in us: by the Spirit He has given us.
passages.sermon:
God gives His Spirit to believers.
Whoever keeps God's commandments lives in God.
God lives in that person.
We know God lives in us because He has given us His Spirit.
passages.original: καὶ ὁ τηρῶν τὰς ἐντολὰς αὐτοῦ ἐν αὐτῷ μένει καὶ αὐτὸς ἐν αὐτῷ καὶ ἐν τούτῳ γινώσκομεν ὅτι μένει ἐν ἡμῖν ἐκ τοῦ Πνεύματος οὗ ἡμῖν ἔδωκεν
